articles.title: What to know about the causes of Spain's latest deadly train crash
articles.description: Spain's second major train collision this year has sparked debate over whether human error or rail network failures are to blame. The transport minister has blamed a traffic controller's poor judgment for Wednesday's crash in Toledo province, which killed 69 people. However, railway unions argue that deteriorating working conditions and failing safety systems are the real issues. A judge and a special government commission are investigating. The collision occurred after a communication system malfunction forced human controllers to manage train safety. Unions say the system, which is being phased out, has failed repeatedly. The crash has raised concerns about increased traffic from rail privatization.

The White House Farm massacre phone calls: could a single disputed digit set Jeremy Bamber free?
articles.description: He has been in prison for 41 years for killing five members of his family. But if a phone call was made to the police by Bamber’s father on the night of the murders – as his team believes – one of the UK’s most notorious criminals could be exonerated On 7 August 1985, five people were found dead at White House Farm in Essex, England: 28-year-old Sheila Caffell (known to her family as Bambi); her six-year-old twin sons, Daniel and Nicholas; and her 61-year-old adoptive parents, June and Nevill Bamber. All five had been shot with a rifle. Caffell’s 24-year-old brother, Jeremy Bamber, who was also adopted, had called to alert Essex police to a disturbance inside the farmhouse – he said his father had called to tell him – and had been outside with the police for four hours before the bodies were discovered. Caffell, who had recently been hospitalised with schizoaffective disorder and is said to have feared her children were going to be taken into foster care, was found with the rifle lying on her chest, pointing towards her neck. There were two gunshot wounds to her neck and chin and a bloodied Bible by her side. The case was initially thought to be open and shut, a tragic murder-suicide committed by Caffell. But a month later, Bamber was arrested after relatives went to the police to voice their suspicions about him; his former girlfriend Julie Mugford then told police he had made a confession to her. The relatives went on to inherit from Nevill and June Bamber’s considerable estate after Bamber’s convictions. It was later discovered that Mugford had agreed to sell the story of their relationship to the News of the World for £25,000 if Bamber was convicted. Essex police and crown prosecutors had also agreed to drop charges against her for burglary, chequebook fraud and selling cannabis, because “prosecuting her could jeopardise her availability or credibility as a key witness” against Bamber. articles.title: Trump erupts in massive late-night golf rant blaming judge if anyone is 'hurt or killed'
articles.description: President Donald Trump took to Truth Social late on Wednesday night to blast the condition of a historic Washington, D.C., golf course in more than 300 words. He said he would hold the federal judge who blocked his renovation plans “fully responsible” if anyone is hurt there. “East Potomac Golf Course is highly dangerous, dilapidated, and absolutely disgusting,” Trump wrote in a post published at 10:43 p.m. ET. “Below are new photos of the deplorable conditions of the driving range building, including excrement in the stairwell.” Trump posted eight photos of the course, showing torn netting, broken railings, exposed rafters, and a patchy, brown driving range. “The gaping holes in the driving range’s ‘protective’ netting are highly hazardous,” he wrote. “Golf balls soar through the holes at high speed and hit unexpecting Golfers—including a White House staffer who was, sadly, hit violently in the chest.” He called the course “a National Disgrace” and a “barren, debris-ridden wasteland.” He promised to turn it into a “WORLD CLASS PUBLIC Golf Course that is AFFORDABLE for locals — Just like the Great and Historic Public Courses of Torrey Pines and Bethpage Black, only better.” Then he turned on the judge. “We will hold the judge, Ana C. Reyes, fully responsible for anybody who is hurt, or killed, on this very dangerous, dilapidated, and unsightly Golf Course,” Trump wrote. Reyes, a Biden appointee on the federal bench in Washington, recently extended an order blocking the administration’s overhaul of the 106-year-old public course, the Associated Press reported. The preliminary injunction bars the government from removing or damaging more trees and requires 10 days’ written notice before any “irreparable modification” to the course while a lawsuit plays out. The suit was brought by the D.C. Preservation League and two golfers after crews cut down at least 400 trees over a holiday weekend with little notice, according to the AP. Trump announced Oct. 18 that he would close the course for 15 months starting Nov. 15 to redevelop it. The administration has said it will appeal, and Reyes rejected its request that she recuse herself.
